1.

The petitioner apprehending arrest in the FIR captioned above has come up before this Court under Section 482 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, [BNSS], seeking anticipatory bail.
2.
In paragraph 18 of the bail petition, the accused declares that he has no criminal antecedents.

3. The facts and allegations are being taken from the short reply filed by the State, which reads as follows:-
"3.

That the brief facts of the present case/FIR No. 143 (supra) are that a complaint dated 17.10.2024 was moved by Fateh Singh (complainant) before Deputy Superintendent of Police, Circle Rajpura, District Patiala, against Charanjit Singh (present petitioner) and his son Jaspreet Singh, with the allegations that Fateh Singh and Jasvir Singh discussed with Charanjit Singh (petitioner) and his son Jaspreet Charanjit Singh vs State Of Punjab And Anr on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/112385545/
1 Singh regarding tourist visa for Europe in August 2023.

entities.text: Jaspreet Charanjit Singh vs State Of Punjab And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The petitioner demanded a sum of Rs. 9,00,000/- from them and assured that he would get them visa for Europe.
For the said purpose, both Fateh Singh and Jasvir Singh transferred a sum of Rs. 7,00,000/- in the bank account of petitioner on different occasions.

Furthermore,
they also gave Rs. 1,00,000/- cash to the petitioner at his house.
After obtaining money, the petitioner told them that their Europe visa authenticity of this order/judgment High Court, Sector 1, Chandigarh CRM-M-60502-2024 would be issued in few days.
During this period, Jaspreet Singh also came from Singapore to the house of complainant and told that he would take them alongwith to Europe.
But Jaspreet Singh first took them to Dubai by telling them that their tickets would be arranged from Dubai.
When they reached at Dubai Airport, Jaspreet Singh demanded more money from them and also threatened that if they would not give him money, then he would not send them to Europe.
The complainant and his accomplice gave Rs. 1,00,000/- to Jaspreet Singh on the spot and thereafter, he ran away from therein.
Thereafter, they stayed at Dubai and one day, they met with Jaspreet Singh and talked to him about money and Europe visa, then Jaspreet Singh brought 4-5 unknown persons and gave them beatings.
He also gave threats to their life and property and told that if they would give more money, then only they could return to India or go to Europe.

Thereafter, the complainant and Jasvir Singh stayed at the house of their friend and with his help,
they came back to India in January 2024.
Whenever, they talk with Jaspreet Singh and Charanjit Singh (petitioner) with regard to visa or money, they gave them life threats.

The petitioner and his son stopped answering the phone calls of the complainants."
4.

The petitioner's counsel prays for bail by imposing any stringent conditions and contends that further pre-trial incarceration would cause an irreversible injustice to the petitioner and their family.
5. The State's counsel opposes bail and refers to the reply.

6. It would be appropriate to refer to the following portions of the reply, which read as follows:
"4. That the enquiry of the said complaint was marked to the office of the answering respondent, who after conducting thorough and detailed enquiry, found that Fateh Singh and Jasvir Singh were intending to go abroad and in this regard, Fateh Singh's brother Bhajan Singh talked with his friend Charanjit Singh (petitioner), who told him that his son Jaspreet Singh was doing the business of sending people abroad.
It was settled by Charanjit Singh (petitioner) and his son Jaspreet Singh to send Fateh Singh and Jasvir Singh to Europe (Germany) for Rs. 9,00,000/-.
Thereafter, Bhajan Singh (complainant's brother) and Jasvir Singh transferred Rs. 7,00,000/- through Google Pay into the account of Jaspreet Singh and Rs. 1,00,000/- cash was given to the petitioner.
They got the visa for Dubai issued to the complainants.

On 03.10.2023, the complainant Fateh Singh and Jasvir Singh went to Dubai from Charanjit Singh vs State Of Punjab And Anr on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/112385545/
2 Chandigarh, wherein they met with Jaspreet Singh at Dubai.

entities.text: Charanjit Singh vs State Of Punjab And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Jaspreet Singh took Rs.
1,00,000/- cash from the complainant at Dubai and Jaspreet Singh kept them with him for 2/3 days and told that after preparing their documents, he would send them to authenticity of this order/judgment High Court, Sector 1, Chandigarh CRM-M-60502-2024 Germany and he kept making excuses to them for 03 months.
Then in January 2023, the complainant party came back to India.
They neither sent the complainant party to Germany nor returning their money.

In this way, Charanjit Singh (petitioner) and his son Jaspreet Singh committed offence under Section 406,
420 of IPC and Section 3 of Human Trafficking Act.

6. ROLE OF PETITIONER:-That the petitioner in connivance with his son Jaspreet Singh (co-accused) obtained a sum of Rs. 9,00,000/- from the complainants Fateh Singh and Jasvir Singh on the pretext of sending them to Germany (Europe) on tourist visa but they neither sent them to Germany (Eupore) not returning their money.
The whole dealing was done by petitioner as his son was at Singapore during that time.
The complainants were sent to Dubai instead wherein they resided for 03 months and finally came back to India in January 2024.
7. EVIDENCE AGAINST PETITIONER:- That the petitioner was specifically named by complainants in their complaint.
Moreover, a sum of Rs. 7,00,000/- was transferred to one Barkat Ali on the asking of petitioner."

7. The petitioner is not the main accused and the only substantial allegation is that he was given a sum of Rs. One Lac, which is not corroborated by any reasons that when the remaining money was transferred through the bank transactions then why Rs One lac was given to the petitioner by cash.
It is not that the petitioner was out of India, where the money transfer would have been cumbersome.
As per the reply, a sum of Rs. Seven Lacs was transferred in the account of Jaspreet Singh.

8. The allegations against the petitioner and the evidence collected against him might be prima facie sufficient to launch prosecution or to frame charges, but this Court is not considering the evidence at that stage but is analyzing it for the stage of anticipatory bail, and an analysis of the allegations and the evidence collected against the petitioner, would not justify custodial interrogation or pre-trial incarceration.
9. Given the above, the penal provisions invoked coupled with the primafacie analysis of the nature of allegations and the other factors peculiar to this case, there would be no justifiability for custodial interrogation or the pre-trial incarceration at this stage, subject to the compliance of terms and conditions mentioned in this order.
Without commenting on the case's merits, in the facts and circumstances peculiar to this case, and for the reasons mentioned above, the petitioner makes a case for bail.
This order shall come into force from the time it is uploaded on this Court's official webpage.
